messages.body_plain:
(R 2.6.0, rJava 0.5.0, OS X)

Hi, I have a Java function whose signature is

 > .jconstructors("org/guha/rcdk/view/ViewMolecule3DDataTable")
[1] "public org.guha.rcdk.view.ViewMolecule3DDataTable 
(java.lang.String[],java.lang.String[],java.lang.Object[][])"


Thus I am trying to send in a data.frame as an Object[][] to this  
function.

If I understand it correctly, to get a 2D array I must sue .jarray  
with a list of arrays.

Thus I have the following code

   rows <- list()
   for (i in 1:nrow(datatable)) {
     row <- list()

     ## for a given row we have to construct a Object[] and add
     ## it to our list
     for (j in 1:ncol(datatable)) {
       if (is.numeric(datatable[i,j])) {
         row[j] <- .jnew("java/lang/Double", datatable[i,j])
       }
       else if (is.character(datatable[i,j])) {
         row[j] <- .jnew("java/lang/String", as.character(datatable 
[i,j]))
       }
     }
     rows[[i]] <- .jarray(row)
   }
   xval.arr <- .jarray(rows)

When I then try and do

  .jnew("org/guha/rcdk/view/ViewMolecule3DTable", farr, carr, xval.arr)

I get the following error

   createObject.GetMethodID("org/guha/rcdk/view/ 
ViewMolecule3DTable","([Ljava/lang/String;[Ljava/lang/String;[Ljava/ 
lang/Object;)V")


If I understand correctly, the Java class is being constructed with a  
Object[] as the third argument. How do I get rJava to give me a Object 
[][] from a set of Object[] refs?

Thanks,

messages.subject: Re: Failied JGR installation on SuSE 10.3
messages.body_plain:
Maura,

It's R that's dying - I have no idea where that assertion comes from.  
I'd suspect some problem in SuSE's X11 libraries ... You may have to  
get a full stack trace (i.e. run R as "R -d gdb" then "r" and when it  
crashes "bt").

You can try to run R without sudo - that will create a temporary  
script, but then please use JGR from rforge as there was a bug in the  
temporary script creating. More precisely install JGR as follows:

sudo R
install.packages("JGR",,"http://www.rforge.net")

Then run R just normally as yourself (without sudo) and type
library(JGR)
JGR()

Cheers,
Simon

See ?.jarray, you have to specify contents.class because you don't  
want it to be java.lang.Object, so it should read something like:
xval.arr <- .jarray(rows, "[Ljava/lang/Object;")

FWIW: the above is very inefficient, I'd hope that the API has a  
provision for arrays ... :P

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject_clean: Quick question on source versions for iPlots
messages.body_plain:
Keith,

On Nov 26, 2007, at 4:57 PM, Keith Sheppard wrote:

> I'm beginning to work with the iPlots java source and I'm a little  
> bit confused by the way the tags directory (http://svn.rforge.net/org/tags/ 
> ) is structured. I don't see release directories that look like the  
> iPlots versions listed here: http://www.rosuda.org/iplots/. Can you  
> recommend a strategy for checking out the most recent/stable version  
> of the java source for iPlots & iPlots dependencies? The source at  
> the trunk doesn't seem to build right now (or I'm just not setting  
> up the build correctly).
>

You should not be using the org repository directly. If you are  
interested in iPlots, you should use the iplots package. You can check  
it out using
svn co svn://svn.rforge.net/iplots/trunk iplots
(see http://www.rforge.net/iplots/svn.html )

For historical reasons we are not using tags to mark iplots releases  
in the svn (it is complicated by the fact that parts of the codebase  
are common to several projects). The policy we use is that the trunk  
is stable unless there is an open branch.

Cheers,
Simon
